title: An scp-like url with an absolute path escapes the public-home, integration and upstream guards, and an unparseable url crashes the pre-push hook
goal: kbpublic.location reads an scp-like url whose path starts with a slash (git@example.com:/org/repo.git) as a remote url, so it matches the https, ssh and other spellings of the same repository in all three guards, excluding only a single-letter Windows drive from the scp form; and a url urllib cannot parse makes location fall back to the url text with no traceback, so the pre-push hook still judges the push and names the url

run: import subprocess,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbpublic;a=kbpublic.location('git@example.com:/org/repo.git','.');b=kbpublic.location('https://example.com/org/repo.git','.');ok=kbpublic.same_repository(a,b);r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-c','import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kbpublic;kbpublic.location("https://[::1/x",".")'],capture_output=True);c=r.returncode==0;print('scp absolute matches https:',ok,'| bad url handled:',c);sys.exit(0 if ok and c else 1)

gates.question: How does location represent a url urllib cannot parse, and how is a scp-like host:/path told from a Windows drive?
options: ('text', url) variant matching only the same text; a one-letter host before a slash is a drive
fall back to a local ('path') location of the url text
gates.recommendation: ('text', url) variant matching only the same text; a one-letter host before a slash is a drive
gates.answer: ('text', url) variant matching only the same text; a one-letter host before a slash is a drive

notes: Found 2026-10-24 by the third SP-3trnelzv review (on 35938e315): SCP_RX's (?![/\\]) lookahead after the colon rejects git@host:/path, so location reads it as a local path; a public-home push spelled that way with a kb/_querylog commit exited 0 through the pre-push hook. The fix excludes only a one-letter drive. S1 by the backlog table (a gate lets a bad push through), so it joins the sprint.
